content:
According to reports, Apple's annual sales in India surpassed US$10 billion for the first time in its last fiscal year.

This achievement is particularly remarkable in a country where the average annual income is less than US$3,000 — especially considering that iPhones are priced higher in India than in the US...

For many years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. But that has changed dramatically in recent years, and with local economic growth, Apple has finally been able to open Apple Stores in the country.

Bloomberg reported this latest milestone today.

Given the low average income and the fact that iPhones are manufactured in India, one might expect local prices to be far lower than in the US. In fact, due to high taxes, Apple products in India are actually priced higher than in the US.

Apple has tried to offset this to some extent by partnering with banks to offer credit card rebates.

About a quarter of iPhones are currently manufactured in India, but most are shipped back to the US for sale. Apple has restructured its logistics arrangements to avoid the tariffs the US imposes on Chinese imports.
